method: Ran each page in Chromium at 1280x900 and 400x850, screenshots at 0.5s, 2s, 5s, at every scroll step and at the footer, plus triggered the share moments (whale typing, held storm press, held Space charge) and compared palette, form legibility, shading ramps and motion across all four with the same sequence.

matter.best: Disciplined heat palette (black, red, orange, gold, white-hot, cold steel blue) and a convincing molten stream plus pool in the hero, with a full-width footer wordmark that glows hot at the top and cools to steel at the bottom.
matter.worst: The giant HTML headline carries the hero and the canvas stays a thin stream and strip; big dead black gaps between sections, and the small button canvases (sand icon, smoke ghost) are tiny and hard to read as forms.
matter.evidence: Hero: bright @ column pouring from a crucible into a banded pool with white-hot surface row and spark particles, drifting between 0.5s and 5s. Footer MELTWORK letters read clearly with a gradient hot-to-cold ramp. Crucible vessel in section 04 reads well. Sections 02 to 03 are mostly text on flat black; the sand icon is about 20 characters wide.

signal.best: The CARRIER wordmark decodes from noise into big, perfectly legible letters with a cyan carrier wave scanning through, and the ASCII world map with amber stations and travelling packets is a genuinely beautiful scene.
signal.worst: Hero canvas has a visible hard horizontal cutoff band around y=345 and is otherwise a mostly empty dark field; cyan on near black with little tonal range makes the page feel one-note, and the ramp swatches/rules section is flat UI.
signal.evidence: At 0.5s the wordmark is half-decoded static in amber; at 5s it is crisp white @ letters with a cyan wave through them. Held Space shows the letters flooded by vertical bars, still legible. Map screenshot shows landmasses shaded with : , . and cyan/amber glints. A hard edge where the hero canvas ends is visible in every hero frame.

sky.best: The whole page is lit by one clock: a sampled gradient sky that moves from dawn pink to noon blue to dusk to a starry night, with cloud ramps, a round sun and moon, birds, rain streaks, and a night Earth with aurora and city lights. It is the only entry where light itself is the art.
sky.worst: Cloud banks are built from fairly repetitive = and + horizontal bands so they read as clouds only from afar, and the translucent dark cards sit on top of busy glyphs and mute the lovely gradient.
sky.evidence: Hero at 0.5s is warm peach to violet; at 5s the MERIDIAN letters are gold glowing @ on a sky already shifting to morning (clock chip 05:46 to 06:43). Afternoon section shows a clearly round sun disc built from @ and % rings. Evening shows glowing horizon fade. Footer night scene with stars, green aurora bars, blue ~ ocean and cloud-covered Earth. Smooth drift between frames, no snapping.

creatures.best: Characters are chosen with directional glyphs (> < ^ v / \), so schools of fish visibly face the way they swim, and jellyfish ((_) / v'v'v), coral and kelp each read as their animal with proper density shading; the reef panel and the dusk to night footer sea are lovely and alive.
creatures.worst: The typed-whale easter egg is a diffuse @ slab that reads as a cloud shape, not a whale, at the moment it appears; hero fish are small and sparse relative to the huge headline; the footer sky is a flat hard-edged CSS color band over the canvas.
creatures.evidence: Hero 2s to 5s: a school of cyan arrow glyphs curls up and to the right toward the cursor, purple jellyfish pulse, coral in coral, lilac and peach at the base. Button cards show orbiting fish, jellyfish and a firefly icon. The reef panel shows layered seabed with green kelp ( ( ) ). In the footer, a hard seam at the pink to blue boundary is visible. The whale frame at 2.5s is mass-of-@ with tail ticks, hard to identify.

one_line_verdict: Sky wins because light and color are the art itself, from a dawn-to-night palette to a round sun and a night Earth, while creatures is a close second with the clearest living forms and matter and signal are strong but thinner as scenes.
